title: Break and Continue
description: Stop a loop early with break, or skip one turn with continue.

content.value: Normally a loop runs every turn from start to finish. Two keywords let you change that. `break` stops the loop completely, and `continue` skips the rest of the current turn and moves on to the next one. Both are usually written inside an `if`, so they only happen in the case you care about.
The two are easy to mix up, so the widget below runs the same loop with each keyword. Switch between them and watch what changes in the trace.
As soon as Python reaches `break`, it leaves the loop entirely. The turns that were still to come never happen at all.
That loop eats cookies 1, 2 and 3, then hits the break on cookie 4 and stops. Cookie 5 is never reached.
`continue` does not stop the loop. It jumps straight to the next turn, skipping whatever was left in the current one. The loop still runs to the end, but one turn does less work than the others.
That loop visits floors 1, 2, 4 and 5. Floor 3 is skipped, but the lift still carries on to the top.
A quick way to remember it: break leaves the building, continue skips a floor.

practice.question: Change the code to print the numbers 1 to 5 but skip the number 3. Replace pass with the right keyword.
Make this loop stop completely once it reaches 4, so it only prints 1, 2 and 3.

quiz.question: Which keyword stops the whole loop right away?
quiz.explain: break leaves the loop completely. continue only skips one turn, and pass does nothing at all.

quiz.question: What does 'continue' do inside a loop?
options: Skips the rest of this turn and starts the next one.
Starts the loop again from the beginning.
quiz.explain: continue skips whatever is left in the current turn and jumps to the next one. The loop itself keeps going.

quiz.question: What does this print?  for i in range(1, 5):  /  if i == 2: continue  /  print(i)
quiz.explain: continue skips only the turn where i is 2. Every other turn prints as normal, so you get 1, 3, 4.
